title: unified-sdk-release-matrix-and-canary-tagging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a unified release matrix and canary tagging workflow for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that supports streaming ergonomics and retry-related examples. Goals: deterministic artifacts, per-language canary channels, atomic multi-package rollouts, and artifact attestations for downstream verification. This ticket covers CI changes, packaging recipes, migration notes for existing clients, and example updates (streaming + retry patterns) that must be included in the release bundle.
acceptance_criteria: CI produces deterministic build artifacts for python/npm/go across supported platforms and records build metadata in a single indexed location
Canary channels are available: npm 'canary' dist-tag, PyPI pre-release wheel with consistent versioning scheme, go module pseudo-versioning and a documented canary import path
Atomic publish step publishes all three SDKs or performs a coordinated rollback if any publish step fails
Artifact attestations (signed build metadata files) are produced and stored alongside releases for security auditing
Shipping examples updated: streaming client example demonstrates ergonomic async streaming and retry hooks for each language
Release notes and migration guide created and linked from console/docs
Release pipeline has automated smoke tests that validate basic generation, streaming, and retry flows post-publish
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off this initiative after last week's release incidents where a partial SDK publish caused client breakage. Drafted initial goals and matrix. See Confluence draft.

2025-02-12 - Connor Morales: Spike completed for deterministic Python wheels using PEP 517 build isolation; identified that linux-manylinux and macosx wheels require reproducible timestamps and recorded hashes. Next: extend to npm tarballs and go module zip artifacts.

2025-02-13 - Design review (Danielle Kim): UX note to surface canary channel names in SDK docs and Console so platform engineers can opt into canaries per-organization. Added doc task to product backlog.

2025-02-14 - Connor Morales: Implemented CI job 'build:snapshot' that emits artifacts into an 'artifact-index' S3 prefix with metadata.json including git sha, build env, and artifact hashes. Pushed branch 'release/matrix-canary'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2142

2025-02-15 - QA (Miguel Santos): Ran smoke tests against the snapshot artifacts. Python wheel import succeeded. npm tarball install had a failing postinstall script — flagged and reverted the script. Item added to follow-ups.

2025-02-16 - Security (Priya Rao): Reviewed attestation approach. Recommended using an in-toto style signed 'attestation.json' per artifact signed with the org release key; will coordinate KMS signing step in CI. Created ticket SEC-274 for key rotation details.

2025-02-17 - Connor Morales: WIP on the atomic publish orchestration: if any language publish step fails, pipeline automatically creates a rollback plan and marks the release candidate as failed. Implemented a dry-run mode for npm and pypi steps. Working on go module publish flow (git tag + push).

2025-02-18 - Product (Lena Wu): Need a short migration note for customers using embedder clients that rely on streaming semantics — ensure example code highlights teardown and retry backoff with idempotency guidance. Assigned to examples owner.
Notes: follow-up tasks include adding Console UI to show active canary releases and linking attestation metadata to release entries.
